title: The Unabomber | The Story of Ted Kaczynski (English Listening Practice)
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，你好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 带来的英语学习播客《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在这里，你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上稀奇古怪、美妙绝伦的事物，同时还能提高你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about The Unabomber.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们将要聊聊 The Unabomber（大学航空炸弹客）。

sentences.en: It's a story of genius, terrorism, isolation, technology, mathematics, and the most expensive manhunt in FBI history.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于天才、恐怖主义、孤立、技术、数学以及 FBI 历史上最昂贵的大搜捕的故事。

sentences.en: OK then, let's not waste a minute and get right into it.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们废话少说，马上开始吧。

sentences.en: The 19th of September, 1995, was a busy day for American newsstands.
sentences.zh: 1995年9月19日，对美国的报摊来说是个忙碌的日子。

sentences.en: From the early morning, up and down the country, queues snaked around the block as people waited in line for their chance to read what promised to be a bombshell story.
sentences.zh: 从清晨开始，全国各地排起了长龙，人们排队等待机会阅读一篇注定会引发轰动的故事。

sentences.en: The Washington Post and the New York Times had announced that they were going to publish, in full, the manifesto of a terrorist killer known only as The Unabomber, a name that came from the FBI’s internal code ‘UNABOM’, short for university and airline bombings..
sentences.zh: 《华盛顿邮报》和《纽约时报》宣布，他们将全文刊登一名被称为 The Unabomber 的恐怖分子的宣言，这个名字来源于联邦调查局的内部代号“UNABOM”，即大学和航空炸弹（university and airline bombings）的缩写。

sentences.en: This decision to publish was unusual for several reasons.
sentences.zh: 决定发表这篇宣言在几个方面都很不寻常。

sentences.en: Firstly, newspapers don’t tend to publish terrorist manifestos.
sentences.zh: 首先，报纸通常不会发表恐怖分子的宣言。

sentences.en: The US government has a stated policy of not cooperating with terrorists, and so agreeing to publish one’s manifesto was unusual, to say the least.
sentences.zh: 美国政府有一项既定政策，即不与恐怖分子合作，因此同意发表某人的宣言，至少可以说是不寻常的。

sentences.en: Secondly, the manifesto was 35,000 words long.
sentences.zh: 其次，这篇宣言长达 35,000 字。

sentences.en: Not exactly coffee shop reading. Thirdly, this manifesto was the first time the general public had heard anything from the Unabomber.
sentences.zh: 这可不是那种在咖啡馆里随手翻阅的读物。第三，这份宣言是公众第一次听到 The Unabomber 的声音。

sentences.en: For 17 years he had been sending anonymous bombs, and this was the first time not just the public, but also the authorities, would understand why.
sentences.zh: 17年来，他一直神出鬼没地邮寄炸弹，而这是公众乃至当局第一次明白他为什么要这么做。

sentences.en: The agreement to publish the manifesto, made with the full approval of the FBI, was a sign of desperation.
sentences.zh: 同意发表这份宣言，是在得到 FBI 全力批准的情况下做出的，这是一个绝望的信号。

sentences.en: Whoever the Unabomber was, he had managed to elude the authorities for the best part of two decades.
sentences.zh: 无论 The Unabomber 是谁，他成功逃避当局追捕的时间将近二十年。

sentences.en: His bombing campaign had started in 1978, and had continued, off and on, until 1995, killing 3 people and injuring an additional 23.
sentences.zh: 他的炸弹袭击始于 1978 年，断断续续一直持续到 1995 年，造成 3 人死亡，23 人受伤。

sentences.en: And for the duration of the campaign, he had never made any requests, not a single demand, nor had he officially claimed responsibility for any of the attacks.
sentences.zh: 在整个袭击期间，他从未提出过任何要求，连一个诉求都没有，也没有官方宣称对任何袭击事件负责。

sentences.en: To state the obvious, this is very unusual; typically a terrorist, or a terrorist group, will put forward demands, or at least they will come forward and claim responsibility for an attack, to try to pressurise a government into taking a particular action.
sentences.zh: 显而易见，这非常不寻常；通常情况下，恐怖分子或恐怖分子组织会提出诉求，或者至少会出面声称对袭击负责，试图施压政府采取某种行动。

sentences.en: The Unabomber had done none of those things.
sentences.zh: The Unabomber 却没有做过其中任何一件事。

sentences.en: Until now. Earlier that year, earlier in 1995, he had written a letter to The New York Times promising to stop the bombings if either the Times or the Washington Post published his manifesto.
sentences.zh: 直到现在。当年早些时候，也就是 1995 年初，他曾给《纽约时报》写过一封信，承诺如果《纽约时报》或《华盛顿邮报》发表他的宣言，他就会停止炸弹袭击。

sentences.en: When this request was taken to the FBI, it was carefully considered.
sentences.zh: 当这个要求呈交给 FBI 时，他们进行了仔细的权衡。

sentences.en: Sure, the United States does not cooperate with terrorists.
sentences.zh: 当然，美国是不会与恐怖分子合作的。

sentences.en: But this wasn’t exactly an impossible demand to agree to; he wasn’t asking for prisoners to be released or for any major change to government policy.
sentences.zh: 但这并非一个无法答应的过分要求；他没有要求释放囚犯，也没有要求对政府政策做出重大改变。

sentences.en: All he wanted was for his views to be published in a major newspaper.
sentences.zh: 他想要的只是把自己的观点发表在一家大报上。

sentences.en: What’s more, after 17 years and thousands of false leads, the FBI was at something of a loss.
sentences.zh: 更何况，在经历了 17 年和数千条错误线索后，FBI 也有点黔驴技穷了。

sentences.en: The bomber had taken meticulous care to cover his tracks, all sorts of psychological profiles had proven to be fruitless, and despite spending today’s equivalent of more than $100 million on the investigation, they were no closer to finding him.
sentences.zh: 炸弹客煞费苦心地抹去行踪，各种心理侧写都被证明是徒劳的，尽管花费了相当于今天超过 1 亿美元的调查资金，他们离找到他依然毫无进展。

sentences.en: So the publication of the manifesto was a gamble —one last attempt to provoke a reaction, to coax the killer into making a mistake, or to encourage someone, anyone, to recognise the voice behind the words.
sentences.zh: 因此，发表这份宣言是一场赌博——这是最后一次试图激起反应、诱使凶手露出破绽，或者鼓励某个人、任何人去听出这些文字背后的声音。

sentences.en: Perhaps, just perhaps, someone might read this manifesto and something might click; a professor reading the style of a former student or a parent recognising their child’s voice from the page.
sentences.zh: 也许，只是也许，会有人读到这份宣言并产生某种共鸣；比如某个教授读出了前学生的风格，或者某个父母从字里行间认出了自己孩子的声音。

sentences.en: If it didn’t work, well, this would be highly embarrassing for the FBI, but they had run out of other options.
sentences.zh: 如果不管用，好吧，这会对 FBI 造成极大的难堪，但他们已经别无选择。

sentences.en: The manifesto began with the now famous line: “The Industrial Revolution and its consequences have been a disaster for the human race."
sentences.zh: 宣言以这句现在已成名言的话开篇：“工业革命及其后果对人类来说是一场灾难。”

sentences.en: And over the next 35,000 words or so, it went on to spell out its author’s worldview, and it was a worldview unlike anything most readers had ever seen printed in a daily newspaper.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的大约 35,000 字中，它阐述了作者的世界观，这是一种大多数读者在日常报纸上从未见过的世界观。

sentences.en: It was bleak, uncompromising, and fiercely argued.
sentences.zh: 它悲观、毫不妥协且论证激烈。

sentences.en: The anonymous author—who signed his letters as “FC”, short for Freedom Club—he believed that modern technological society was not simply flawed, but fundamentally incompatible with human freedom.
sentences.zh: 这位匿名作者——他在信中署名“FC”，即自由俱乐部（Freedom Club）的缩写——他认为现代技术社会不仅有瑕疵，而且与人类的自由根本水火不容。

sentences.en: Technology, he argued, did not liberate us; it enslaved us.
sentences.zh: 他辩称，技术并没有解放我们；而是奴役了我们。

sentences.en: The more complex our systems became, the more dependent we grew on them, and the more powerless the individual became in the face of governments, corporations, and machines.
sentences.zh: 我们的系统变得越复杂，我们对它们的依赖就越深，个体在政府、公司和机器面前就越无力。

sentences.en: This wasn’t the disjointed ramblings you might expect from a mad serial killer.
sentences.zh: 这并不是你可能会从一个疯狂的连环杀手那里听到的那种语无伦次胡言乱语。

sentences.en: It was disturbingly rational. Logical. Eloquent.
sentences.zh: 它令人不安地理性。逻辑严密。文笔流畅。

sentences.en: This was clearly the work of a brilliant mind.
sentences.zh: 这显然是一个极其聪明的人的手笔。

sentences.en: Yes, someone prepared to kill, a murderer.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个随时准备杀戮的凶手。

sentences.en: But it was logically set out, touched on political theory, sociology, psychology, and history, and it displayed a truly encyclopedic knowledge.
sentences.zh: 但它逻辑清晰，触及了政治理论、社会学、心理学和历史，并展现了堪称百科全书般的广博知识。

sentences.en: The Unabomber was extraordinary in the literal sense of the word.
sentences.zh: The Unabomber 是字面意义上的不同寻常（extraordinary）。

sentences.en: The manifesto was published, and, true to his word, the bombings stopped.
sentences.zh: 宣言发表了，正如他所承诺的那样，炸弹袭击停止了。

sentences.en: The FBI and the government had honoured their side of the deal, and the Unabomber honoured his.
sentences.zh: FBI 和政府履行了他们的承诺，The Unabomber 也兑现了他的承诺。

sentences.en: As the authorities hoped, the phones started ringing off the hook.
sentences.zh: 正如当局所期望的那样，电话开始响个不停。

sentences.en: Every lead was followed up on, but it came to nothing.
sentences.zh: 每一条线索都被跟进，但最终都无果而终。

sentences.en: However, in the small town of Schenectady, New York, one man read the manifesto and a terrible, sinking feeling came over him.
sentences.zh: 然而，在纽约斯克内克塔迪小镇，一个人读了这份宣言，一种可怕、沉重的感觉涌上心头。

sentences.en: His name was David Kaczynski, and he had been persuaded to read the manifesto by his wife, Linda.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫大卫·卡钦斯基（David Kaczynski），在妻子琳达的劝说下，他读了这份宣言。

sentences.en: See, David had an older brother, Theodore, or Ted, for short.
sentences.zh: 你看，大卫有一个哥哥，叫西奥多，简称泰德（Ted）。

sentences.en: Linda had never met Ted, but she had heard all about him.
sentences.zh: 琳达从未见过泰德，但她听过很多关于他的事。

sentences.en: The two brothers had been very close, and although David hadn’t seen Ted for a long time, they had kept in touch by letter.
sentences.zh: 兄弟俩曾经非常亲密，虽然大卫很久没见泰德了，但他们一直通过书信保持联系。

sentences.en: Ted, so David believed, was living as a recluse in an isolated cabin in the wilds of Montana, cut off from the modern world.
sentences.zh: 在大卫看来，泰德一直像个隐士一样住在蒙大拿州荒野中一个与世隔绝的小木屋里，与现代社会隔绝。

sentences.en: From what Linda had heard about her brother-in-law, well, it sounded quite similar to what she had read in the press about the Unabomber.
sentences.zh: 根据琳达从媒体上听到的关于她大伯子的事，嗯，这听起来和她在媒体上读到的关于 The Unabomber 的描述非常相似。

sentences.en: “Just read the manifesto”, she told her husband.
sentences.zh: “读读这份宣言吧，”她对丈夫说。

sentences.en: “For me”. Reluctantly, David Kaczynski picked up the newspaper.
sentences.zh: “为了我。”大卫·卡钦斯基不情愿地拿起报纸。

sentences.en: Almost immediately, he recognised the voice, the intense, almost obsessive way of arguing, the deep-seated hatred of technology, even certain specific and unusual expressions and turns of phrase that he knew his brother used.
sentences.zh: 几乎立刻，他就认出了那个声音、那种强烈且几乎带有强迫症的辩论方式、对科技根深蒂固的仇恨，甚至还有他知道他哥哥用过的一些特定且不寻常的表达和措辞。

sentences.en: His worst fears were confirmed; to David Kaczynski, it was undeniable that the author of the Unabomber’s Manifesto and his older brother, Ted, were the same person.
sentences.zh: 他最担忧的事情得到了证实；对大卫·卡钦斯基来说，Unabomber 宣言的作者和他的哥哥泰德毫无疑问是同一个人。

sentences.en: Instead of immediately going to the FBI, he decided to first hire a private investigator, then a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 他没有直接去找 FBI，而是决定先雇佣一名私家侦探，然后是一位律师。

sentences.en: He didn’t want to go straight to the authorities; he knew his brother might be in a fragile mental state, and he didn’t want a raid resulting in him getting shot.
sentences.zh: 他不想直接去找当局；他知道他哥哥的精神状态可能很脆弱，他不想因为突袭搜查而导致他被枪击。

sentences.en: The private investigator compared writing samples, samples of Ted’s letters to his brother with the Unabomber’s manifesto.
sentences.zh: 私家侦探对比了笔迹样本，将泰德写给他弟弟的信件样本与 The Unabomber 的宣言进行了比对。

sentences.en: She determined that it was highly likely to be a match.
sentences.zh: 她断定极有可能是同一个人。

sentences.en: Early in 1996, David presented the information to the FBI, but demanded assurances that it would be an anonymous tip-off; the last thing he wanted was for his brother to know that it was him.
sentences.zh: 1996 年初，大卫将这些信息交给了 FBI，但要求保证这是一个匿名举报；他最不希望的就是让哥哥知道举报人是他。

sentences.en: See, Ted and David had been very close, so close, in fact, that David still found it almost impossible to believe that the boy that he had grown up with—a shy, brilliant child who had once spent hours teaching him maths puzzles—that this boy could be responsible for such cold-blooded violence.
sentences.zh: 要知道，泰德和大卫曾经非常亲密，事实上亲密到大卫仍然觉得几乎无法相信，那个和他一起长大的男孩——一个曾经花几个小时教他数学谜题的害羞、聪明的孩子——竟然会做出如此冷血的暴力行径。

sentences.en: So to understand why this was so painful, and what might have caused Ted Kaczynski to behave in this way, we need to go back to his early life.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了理解为什么这如此痛苦，以及是什么导致泰德·卡钦斯基会有这样的表现，我们需要追溯到他的早年生活。

sentences.en: He was born in Chicago in 1942 into what seemed, from the outside, like a perfectly ordinary, hard-working, Polish American family.
sentences.zh: 他 1942 年出生于芝加哥，在外人看来，那是一个极其普通、勤劳的波兰裔美国家庭。

sentences.en: His parents ran a small sausage factory; they were not wealthy, but they put a high value on education and they quickly realised that their eldest son was not like other children.
sentences.zh: 他的父母经营着一家小型香肠厂；他们并不富有，但他们非常看重教育，并且很快意识到他们的大儿子和其他孩子不一样。

sentences.en: He was off-the-charts intelligent. By the age of six, Ted was doing complex arithmetic in his head.
sentences.zh: 他的智商高得离谱。六岁时，泰德就能在脑海里做复杂的算术。

sentences.en: By eight, he was reading advanced scientific material for fun.
sentences.zh: 八岁时，他为了好玩而阅读高级科学资料。

sentences.en: By ten, he had scored so highly on an IQ test, getting a mark of 167, that psychologists recommended he skip not just one year of school, but two.
sentences.zh: 十岁时，他在智商测试中获得了 167 分的高分，以至于心理学家建议他不仅要跳级一年，而是跳级两年。

sentences.en: This decision would shape the rest of his life.
sentences.zh: 这个决定将塑造他余下的人生。

sentences.en: Skipping grades might have made academic sense, but socially it was a disaster.
sentences.zh: 跳级在学业上可能合乎情理，但在社交上却是一场灾难。

sentences.en: Ted was smaller, younger, and far more sensitive than the older boys in his new class.
sentences.zh: 泰德比他新班级里的那些大男孩更瘦小、更年轻，也敏感得多。

sentences.en: He struggled to fit in, struggled to make new friends, and began to retreat into the one world in which he felt safe: mathematics.
sentences.zh: 他努力融入集体，努力交新朋友，并开始退缩到他感到安全的唯一世界里：数学。

sentences.en: His teachers described him as “quiet”, “withdrawn”, even “timid”.
sentences.zh: 他的老师形容他“安静”、“内向”，甚至“胆小”。

sentences.en: But in maths class he came alive. Numbers somehow made sense when people did not.
sentences.zh: 但在数学课上，他整个人都生动了起来。当人们让人难以理解时，数字不知怎么地总是讲得通。

sentences.en: When he was just sixteen years old, he was encouraged to apply to, and was accepted into Harvard, becoming one of the youngest students ever admitted.
sentences.zh: 就在他十六岁时，他被鼓励申请哈佛大学并被录取，成为了哈佛录取的年纪最小的学生之一。

sentences.en: For most families this would have been a dream come true.
sentences.zh: 对大多数家庭来说，这绝对是梦想成真。

sentences.en: But for Ted, who was still very much a child on an emotional level, Harvard was not a dream.
sentences.zh: 但对泰德来说，他在情感上依然只是个孩子，哈佛并不是梦想。

sentences.en: It was overwhelming, isolating, and sometimes traumatic.
sentences.zh: 那是压倒性的、孤立的，有时甚至是痛苦的。

sentences.en: During his first year, he participated in a now-infamous psychological study run by a Harvard professor named Henry Murray.
sentences.zh: 在大一期间，他参加了一项现在声名狼藉的心理学研究，该研究由哈佛教授亨利·默里（Henry Murray）主持。

sentences.en: This study involved long, aggressive interrogation sessions designed to break down the participants’ beliefs.
sentences.zh: 这项研究涉及长期、具有攻击性的审讯环节，旨在瓦解参与者的信念。

sentences.en: Kaczynski would later describe it as deeply humiliating, and subsequent commentators have suggested that it left lasting psychological scars on the young man.
sentences.zh: 卡钦斯基后来将其描述为极具羞辱性，后来的评论者也暗示这给这个年轻人留下了持久的心理创伤。

sentences.en: From Harvard he moved on to graduate studies, eventually earning a PhD in mathematics at the University of Michigan when he was only 25 years old.
sentences.zh: 从哈佛毕业后，他继续深造，最终在 25 岁时获得了密歇根大学的数学博士学位。

sentences.en: His thesis was so advanced that, according to someone on his dissertation panel, "maybe 10 or 12 men in the country understood or appreciated it."
sentences.zh: 他的论文是如此先进，以至于根据他论文答辩委员会成员的说法，“全国大概只有 10 到 12 个人能理解或欣赏它。”

sentences.en: It seemed to his professors that he was destined to become one of the great American mathematicians of his generation.
sentences.zh: 他的教授们觉得，他注定要成为他那一代伟大的美国数学家之一。

sentences.en: And yet, in 1969, something extraordinary happened.
sentences.zh: 然而，在 1969 年，发生了一件非同寻常的事。

sentences.en: At the age of 27, after accepting a prestigious teaching position at Berkeley, Ted Kaczynski suddenly resigned.
sentences.zh: 27 岁时，在接受了加州大学伯克利分校的一份声誉卓著的教职后，泰德·卡钦斯基突然辞职了。

sentences.en: He walked away from a seemingly secure academic career, from a life that most people would consider incredibly successful.
sentences.zh: 他放弃了一个看似稳定的学术生涯，放弃了大多数人认为极其成功的生活。

sentences.en: And he simply disappeared, or at least withdrew completely from society.
sentences.zh: 他索性消失了，或者说彻底退出了社会。

sentences.en: He moved to a patch of remote land outside the tiny town of Lincoln, Montana, where he built, with his own hands, a tiny wooden cabin.
sentences.zh: 他搬到了蒙大拿州小镇林肯郊外的一片偏远土地上，在那里亲手建造了一间小木屋。

sentences.en: No electricity. No running water. No telephone.
sentences.zh: 没有电。没有自来水。没有电话。

sentences.en: No car. No neighbours. Just trees, mountains, and silence.
sentences.zh: 没有汽车。没有邻居。只有树木、高山和寂静。

sentences.en: It was here, in the solitude of the Montana woods, that Ted believed he could finally think clearly.
sentences.zh: 正是在这里，在蒙大拿树林的孤独中，泰德相信他终于可以清晰地思考了。

sentences.en: Here, he would be free from the modern world he feared and hated.
sentences.zh: 在这里，他将摆脱他所恐惧和恨之入骨的现代世界。

sentences.en: Here, he could live entirely independently, growing vegetables, trapping animals, reading philosophy, and writing page after page of notes on the dangers of technology.
sentences.zh: 在这里，他可以完全独立地生活，种蔬菜、设陷阱捕猎动物、阅读哲学，并写下一页又一页关于技术危害的笔记。

sentences.en: But this isolation did not calm him; it radicalised him.
sentences.zh: 但这种孤立并没有让他平静下来；反而让他变得激进。

sentences.en: He watched the forests around him being cut down by developers; he saw aircraft flying overhead, he heard the distant hum of industrial progress, and grew convinced that technology was spreading like a disease.
sentences.zh: 他看着身边的森林被开发商砍伐；他看到飞机从头顶飞过，听到远处工业进步的嗡嗡声，并坚信技术正像疾病一样蔓延。

sentences.en: In his journals he wrote that the modern world was “robbing people of their freedom”, that industrial society was “crushing the human spirit”.
sentences.zh: 他在日记中写道，现代世界正在“剥夺人们的自由”，工业社会正在“粉碎人类的精神”。

sentences.en: By the mid-1970s, Ted Kaczynski had transformed from a gifted mathematician into an ideological extremist.
sentences.zh: 到 20 世纪 70 年代中期，泰德·卡钦斯基已经从一个天才数学家蜕变为一个思想激进分子。

sentences.en: And in 1978, he made a decision that would change everything.
sentences.zh: 1978 年，他做出了一个将改变一切的决定。

sentences.en: He built a bomb. It was hand-crafted from metal tubing, wood, batteries, and homemade components, it was placed in a parcel and left in a hallway at Northwestern University.
sentences.zh: 他制造了一枚炸弹。它由金属管、木头、电池和自制组件手工制成，被装在一个包裹里，放在西北大学的一个走廊里。

sentences.en: When it exploded, injuring a security officer, his 17-year campaign of violence had begun.
sentences.zh: 当它爆炸并炸伤一名保安时，他长达 17 年的暴力行动开始了。

sentences.en: Over the next decade and a half he mailed or delivered a series of increasingly sophisticated bombs, each designed to maim or kill, each carefully constructed to leave almost no usable forensic evidence.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的十五年里，他邮寄或投递了一系列日益复杂的炸弹，每一个都旨在致残或杀害，每一个都经过精心构造，几乎不留下任何可用的法医证据。

sentences.en: And his methods were meticulous. He sanded off fingerprints.
sentences.zh: 他的作案手法极其严密。他打磨掉指纹。

sentences.en: He used handmade wooden parts to avoid traceability.
sentences.zh: 他使用手工制作的木质零件以避免被追踪。

sentences.en: He built explosive components from scratch.
sentences.zh: 他从零开始制造爆炸物组件。

sentences.en: He included false clues, misleading markings, fake initials, random pieces of metal or hair he had found in public bathrooms, all intended to confuse investigators.
sentences.zh: 他故意留下虚假的线索、具有误导性的标记、伪造的主题首字母、在公共卫生间找到的随机金属碎片或头发，所有这些都是为了迷惑调查人员。

sentences.en: Some bombs were disguised as parcels, others as pieces of scientific equipment.
sentences.zh: 有些炸弹伪装成包裹，有些伪装成科学仪器。

sentences.en: One of his early devices was planted on an American Airlines flight, causing smoke to fill the cabin and nearly forcing an emergency landing.
sentences.zh: 他早期的装置之一被安放在一架美国航空公司的航班上，导致浓烟弥漫机舱，差点逼迫飞机紧急迫降。

sentences.en: Another killed a computer store owner in Sacramento.
sentences.zh: 另一枚炸弹炸死了一家萨克拉门托的电脑店老板。

sentences.en: Another left a university professor permanently disabled.
sentences.zh: 还有一枚让一名大学教授终身残疾。

sentences.en: The authorities at first couldn’t figure out the connection between these people.
sentences.zh: 当局起初无法找出这些人之间的联系。

sentences.en: Professors, airline executives, computer store owners, there seemed to be nothing linking them.
sentences.zh: 教授、航空公司高管、电脑店老板，他们之间似乎没有任何联系。

sentences.en: The connection was technology; these were people Kaczynski believed were responsible for advancing the technological society he so despised.
sentences.zh: 唯一的联系就是技术；这些人都是卡钦斯基认为应对推进他所鄙视的技术社会负责的人。

sentences.en: When it became clear that this was the work of a sophisticated terrorist, the FBI launched what would become the longest and most expensive manhunt in its history.
sentences.zh: 当明显这是一起由高智商恐怖分子制造的案件时，FBI 发起了其历史上历时最长、耗资最大的一场大搜捕。

sentences.en: And yet, for years, they had nothing. No suspect.
sentences.zh: 然而，多年来，他们一无所获。没有嫌疑人。

sentences.en: No motive. No pattern they could reliably identify.
sentences.zh: 没有动机。没有他们能可靠识别的模式。

sentences.en: To the authorities, the Unabomber was not simply dangerous; he was invisible.
sentences.zh: 在当局看来，The Unabomber 不仅危险，而且隐形。

sentences.en: And it probably would have stayed that way if not for the publication of the manifesto, and the moment David Kaczynski recognised the voice of his brother.
sentences.zh: 如果不是因为那份宣言的发表，以及大卫·卡钦斯基认出他哥哥声音的那个时刻，情况可能还会一直这样下去。

sentences.en: Now, when the FBI received the tip, they were initially skeptical.
sentences.zh: 现在，当 FBI 收到这条线索时，他们起初是持怀疑态度的。

sentences.en: They had received thousands of similar leads over the years—tips from people suspecting neighbours, colleagues, or even family members—and all had been dead ends.
sentences.zh: 多年来，他们收到了数千条类似的线索——来自怀疑邻居、同事甚至家庭成员的举报——结果全都是死胡同。

sentences.en: But this one was different. The FBI had a number of letters and documents written by the Unabomber, and when they compared them to the old letters and academic papers written by Ted Kaczynski, the similarities were striking.
sentences.zh: 但这一条不同。FBI 手头有许多由 The Unabomber 撰写信件和文件，当他们将这些与泰德·卡钦斯基过去写的信件和学术论文进行对比时，惊人的相似之处显现出来。

sentences.en: They used a technique called forensic linguistics, which is the study of language in a legal context, and the experts noted identical usages of certain uncommon words and specific, idiosyncratic grammatical constructions.
sentences.zh: 他们使用了一种叫做司法语言学（forensic linguistics）的技术，这是在法律背景下对语言的研究，专家们注意到某些不常见词汇的相同用法以及特定的、独特的语法结构。

sentences.en: With mounting evidence, the FBI obtained a search warrant for Ted Kaczynski's cabin in Montana.
sentences.zh: 随着证据越来越多，FBI 获得了搜查泰德·卡钦斯基在蒙大拿州木屋的搜查令。

sentences.en: They knew that they had to catch him red-handed; other than the similarities in writing styles, they had nothing concrete linking him to the crimes.
sentences.zh: 他们知道他们必须人赃俱获；除了文风相似之外，他们没有确凿的证据将他与犯罪联系起来。

sentences.en: The cabin was their last hope. On April 3, 1996, a team of FBI agents arrived on the scene.
sentences.zh: 木屋是他们最后的希望。1996 年 4 月 3 日，一队 FBI 特工抵达现场。

sentences.en: Posing as forestry workers, they knocked on the door.
sentences.zh: 他们伪装成林业工人，敲响了房门。

sentences.en: A dishevelled but importantly unarmed Kaczynski opened, and was swiftly arrested.
sentences.zh: 一个衣衫不整但关键是手无寸铁的卡钦斯基打开了门，随即被迅速逮捕。

sentences.en: And a search of the cabin revealed everything the FBI was looking for.
sentences.zh: 对木屋的搜查揭示了 FBI 寻找的一切。

sentences.en: They found a wealth of evidence, including four fully constructed and ready-to-mail bombs, and the original, handwritten draft of the 35,000-word manifesto.
sentences.zh: 他们发现了丰富的证据，包括四枚完全组装好、准备邮寄的炸弹，以及那份 35,000 字宣言的原始手写草稿。

sentences.en: Alongside this, there were detailed journals containing the formula and process for every single one of the 16 bombings the Unabomber had carried out.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，还有详细的日记，里面记录了 The Unabomber 实施的全部 16 起爆炸案中每一起的公式和过程。

sentences.en: These weren’t written in plain English, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，这些并没有用普通的英语写成。

sentences.en: Kaczynski had encrypted them using an incredibly sophisticated system of codes, but fortunately for the authorities, the ciphers, the codes to decipher the system, were also found in the cabin.
sentences.zh: 卡钦斯基用一套极其复杂的密码系统对它们进行了加密，但幸运的是，解密这些系统的密码本也在木屋里被找到了。

sentences.en: Ted Kaczynski was arrested. The man who had been the subject of the most complex, long-running, and expensive investigation in US history was finally in custody.
sentences.zh: 泰德·卡钦斯基被捕了。这个美国历史上最复杂、历时最长、耗资最大的调查对象终于落网了。

sentences.en: But the story doesn't end there. The trial, and the ultimate fate of this boy-genius-turned-terrorist, would raise profound questions about responsibility, mental health, and the very nature of modern society.
sentences.zh: 但故事并没有就此结束。审判以及这位天才少年变成的恐怖分子的最终命运，将引发关于责任、心理健康以及现代社会本质的深刻问题。

sentences.en: Ted Kaczynski never denied being The Unabomber, but his legal defense was complicated.
sentences.zh: 泰德·卡钦斯基从未否认自己是 The Unabomber，但他的法律辩护很复杂。

sentences.en: His lawyers wanted to argue that he was mentally ill and therefore not responsible for his actions.
sentences.zh: 他的律师想辩称他患有精神疾病，因此不承担责任。

sentences.en: They wanted him to plead "not guilty by reason of insanity."
sentences.zh: 他们希望他以“精神失常导致无罪”进行抗辩。

sentences.en: In other words, he was crazy. Kaczynski, however, fiercely objected to this strategy.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他是个疯子。然而，卡钦斯基强烈反对这一策略。

sentences.en: He saw himself not as a madman, but as a rational revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 他认为自己不是疯子，而是理性的革命者。

sentences.en: To be declared insane would invalidate his manifesto and his entire political philosophy, and the entire reason he had embarked on his bombing campaign was for his views to be taken seriously.
sentences.zh: 被宣布为精神失常将使他的宣言和他的整个政治哲学化为乌有，而他之所以踏上炸弹袭击之路，其全部原因就是为了让自己的观点被严肃对待。

sentences.en: He was so determined that he eventually tried to fire his own defense team and represent himself in court.
sentences.zh: 他如此坚定，以至于最终试图解雇自己的辩护团队，并在法庭上为自己辩护。

sentences.en: In the end, he avoided a potentially lengthy and highly publicised trial by accepting a plea bargain.
sentences.zh: 最后，他通过接受认罪协议，避免了一场可能旷日持久且备受瞩目的审判。

sentences.en: On January 22, 1998, Ted Kaczynski pleaded guilty to all charges.
sentences.zh: 1998 年 1 月 22 日，泰德·卡钦斯基对所有指控表示认罪。

sentences.en: In exchange for avoiding the death penalty, he was sentenced to eight consecutive life sentences without the possibility of parole.
sentences.zh: 作为免于死刑的交换，他被判处八个连续终身监禁，且不得假释。

sentences.en: He was transferred to the Supermax prison in Florence, Colorado, where he lived out the remainder of his days, much of it in solitary confinement, before finally killing himself in June of 2023, at the age of 81.
sentences.zh: 他被转移到科罗拉多州佛罗伦萨的超级最高安全监狱（Supermax），在那里度过了余生，其中大部分时间都在单人牢房中度过，直到最后在 2023 年 6 月自杀身亡，享年 81 岁。

sentences.en: And there is another twist to this story.
sentences.zh: 这个故事还有一个反转。

sentences.en: His bombing spree started in 1978, in a world we might today consider relatively free from technology.
sentences.zh: 他的炸弹袭击始于 1978 年，在一个我们今天可能认为相对没有技术干扰的世界里。

sentences.en: Today, where technology is infinitely more entrenched in every aspect of our lives than 50 years ago, his anti-technology message is able to spread ever further and faster, and is reaching more people than ever before.
sentences.zh: 今天，科技比 50 年前更深地融入了我们生活的方方面面，他的反科技信息得以传得更远、更快，正触及比以往任何时候都多的人。

sentences.en: Whether it’s simply that his manifesto is easily accessible online, or that people are making TikToks about “Uncle Ted was right”, his worldview and philosophy is becoming more and more well-known through the very technology he sought to destroy.
sentences.zh: 不管是他的宣言在网上很容易找到，还是人们在 TikTok 上制作关于“泰德叔叔是对的”的视频，他的世界观和哲学正通过他试图摧毁的这项技术变得越来越广为人知。

sentences.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode on The Unabomber.
sentences.zh: 好了，关于 The Unabomber 的这一期节目就到这里。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 希望这期节目对你有所启发，让你学到了新东西。

sentences.en: As always, I'd love to know what you thought of this episode.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样，我很想知道你对这期节目的看法。

sentences.en: For the members among you, you can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 如果是我们的会员，你可以直接访问我们的社区论坛，网址是 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他好奇的灵魂畅所欲言。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是由 Leonardo English 带来的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，注意安全，我们下期节目再见。
